title: Quasi-coherent space modules are closed under kernels and small colimits
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use the small etale module category and quasi-coherence of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. If $f:M\to N$ is a map of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules, its kernel and cokernel in all module sheaves are quasi-coherent. Every small diagram of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules has a colimit in all module sheaves, and this colimit is quasi-coherent. Thus the full inclusion $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ preserves these kernels, cokernels and small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. In particular arbitrary small direct sums and images of maps between quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent. No Noetherian or separation hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Work in the small-site universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. The ambient module categories have all small colimits and are abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $p:U\to X$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For any etale scheme chart $V\to X$, its ringed slice is $V_{\mathrm{et}}$: by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests] every scheme map $W\to V$ over $X$ between etale charts is etale, and conversely an etale $W\to V$ composes to an etale chart $W\to X$; coverings are jointly surjective etale families on both sides, and structure-ring values are $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$. Write $r_V$ for restriction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction] to the representable sheaf of $V$: its element site is exactly this slice, so $r_V$ is exact. Its geometric localization morphism has unchanged coefficient ring. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] makes $r_V$ a left adjoint, and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] gives preservation of every small colimit, including cokernels and sums. Exactness gives $r_V\ker f=\ker(r_Vf)$.

proof.text: The local-presentation predicate [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] is preserved by restriction to any slice: pull a presentation cover back along each slice object and use relocalization [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Conversely, suppose $r_UM$ is quasi-coherent. For each $V\to X$, the base change $V\times_XU$ is a scheme, its projection to $V$ is surjective etale and its composite to $X$ is etale [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], so $V\times_XU\to V$ is a covering in the small etale site, by representability and surjectivity of the atlas [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Cover this object further by the local-presentation cover for $r_UM$ on $V\times_XU\to U$. These presentations are precisely presentations of $M$ on the same objects over $V$, by the sectionwise restriction and relocalization formulas. The composite family is a cover. Thus $M$ satisfies the predicate on every $V$, so is quasi-coherent. This proves explicitly the detection needed below.

First establish the scheme small-etale case. For any scheme $T$, [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies quasi-coherent etale modules with Zariski quasi-coherent modules by a fully faithful equivalence $A_T$, and identifies $A_T$ with tensor pullback for the canonical ringed-site morphism. A diagram lifts to a Zariski diagram by the inverse equivalence; full faithfulness supplies all arrows and their functor laws. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] this tensor pullback, on all Zariski module sheaves, is left adjoint to module direct image. It therefore preserves all small colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. The ambient Zariski and etale module categories admit these colimits by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian].

For completeness the Zariski colimit just used is quasi-coherent. Let $L$ be the ambient colimit of a small diagram $G_i$ of quasi-coherent modules on $T$. Restriction to an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ preserves the colimit and quasi-coherence by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], write this restricted diagram as $\widetilde{E_i}$, including its arrows, using the natural counit isomorphisms. The $B$-module diagram has a colimit $E$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian]. The same tilde adjunction says $\widetilde E$ is an ambient colimit of $\widetilde{E_i}$. Uniqueness of colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $L|_W\simeq\widetilde E$, which is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. The affine-local definition [pqf-def-coherent] proves quasi-coherence of $L$. Step 3 now shows that any small colimit of quasi-coherent modules on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ is $A_T(L)$ and is quasi-coherent.

For scheme small-etale kernels use [lem-trf-scheme-etale-quasi-coherent-kernel]. For cokernels, lift a map to a Zariski map by the full faithfulness in [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Its Zariski cokernel is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image]. Applying the colimit-preserving tensor pullback of step 3 identifies its image with the ambient small-etale cokernel. Thus both operations on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ preserve quasi-coherence, with no finiteness hypothesis.

Let $f:M\to N$ be a morphism of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $D:I\to\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ any small diagram. Form $K=\ker f$, $Q=\operatorname{coker}f$, and $C=\operatorname{colim}_I D$ in ambient modules (step 1). Their restrictions to $U$ are respectively the kernel, cokernel, and colimit of the restricted inputs (step 1). Those inputs are quasi-coherent by step 2. Steps 4 and 5 on the scheme $U$ therefore show that $r_UK,r_UQ,r_UC$ are quasi-coherent. The explicit detection in step 2 shows that $K,Q,C$ are quasi-coherent on $X$. This is exactly the atlas reduction of Tag 03M1; it uses neither quasi-compactness, separation nor Noetherianity.

Because [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] defines $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ as a full subcategory, each ambient universal property remains valid when its test objects are restricted to quasi-coherent ones. The objects just proved quasi-coherent therefore also give the kernels, cokernels and colimits in that full subcategory, and the inclusion preserves them. A small direct sum is a discrete small colimit. In the ambient abelian module category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the image is $\ker(N\to\operatorname{coker}f)$, so is quasi-coherent by the kernel and cokernel assertions already proved. This also handles the empty colimit and the zero map.
